construct: Under normoxia, prolyl hydroxylase domain enzymes use molecular oxygen to hydroxylate conserved proline residues on HIF-alpha. Hydroxylated HIF-alpha is recognized by the VHL-containing E3 ubiquitin-ligase complex, ubiquitinated, and degraded by the proteasome. Hypoxia inhibits prolyl hydroxylation, stabilizing HIF-alpha and permitting transcription of hypoxia-responsive genes.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Selective inhibition of HIF prolyl hydroxylase at normoxia prevents the hydroxylation signal required for pVHL binding, so downstream VHL recognition and ubiquitination fall while HIF-alpha mRNA and proteasome function remain intact.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Proteasomal degradation is tempting because HIF-alpha accumulates, but the stem explicitly preserves proteasome function; the blocked regulatory event is the upstream hydroxylation-dependent VHL recognition and ubiquitination step.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Only the keyed downstream event directly depends on prior PHD-mediated prolyl hydroxylation and explains protein stabilization without an mRNA increase.
